opening.analysis: future active indicative third singular; he/she will bring; masculine referent inferred from context, not finite-verb gender

approach.analysis: aorist active participle masculine nominative singular; naturally construed with explicit priest in following verse

syriac.analysis_basis: CAL stem tag plus our analysis of displayed surface

syriac.analysis: Pael imperfect second masculine singular in context with third-masculine-singular object; to the priest gives destination
syriac.analysis_basis: CAL stem tag plus our contextual inflectional analysis, not a CAL person tag

syriac.analysis: Aphel imperfect third masculine singular with third-masculine-singular object; receiving priest naturally inferred as agent

aroma_control.cal_warning: Lexical parsing is stored jointly with adjacent variant; the series contains more than one reading.
aroma_control.conclusion: Greek aroma phrase and Syriac lexical alternative do not recover presence/absence of Hebrew medial waw. No aroma English change selected from orthography.

comparison_outcomes.opening_selective_report: Publisher Greek third singular and CAL contextual second singular support the earlier EG-CONT-03 versional alignment at this local locus.
comparison_outcomes.later_clauses: CAL delivery is second person in context whereas stored WLC pointing is third masculine singular. The opening alignment must not be extended to all clauses. Greek approach crosses verse boundary.
comparison_outcomes.hebrew_retroversion: No unique Vorlage reconstructed; translation syntax, morphology and harmonization remain possible explanations.
comparison_outcomes.witness_count: Publisher and OpenScriptorium are edition-family controls, not two Greek physical manuscripts. CAL and the Leiden edition it derives from are not two physical witnesses. Neither names a newly inspected physical witness at the target.
